questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "I ___ dinner when the phone rang."
questions.explanation: Use the past continuous for a longer action that was in progress when a shorter action (past simple) interrupted it.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "As soon as the bell rang, the students ___ the classroom."
questions.explanation: Use the past simple for a completed action that happened right after another one ("as soon as" shows a sequence).

questions.prompt: This sentence is correct: "I was knowing the answer, but I didn't say anything."
questions.explanation: Stative verbs like "know" are not normally used in continuous forms. The correct sentence is "I knew the answer, but I didn't say anything."

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "This time yesterday, we ___ on a beach in Spain."
questions.explanation: Use the past continuous for an action in progress at a specific time in the past, such as "this time yesterday".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "She ___ her ankle while she was playing tennis."
questions.explanation: The short, sudden event uses the past simple ("hurt"); the longer background action uses the past continuous ("was playing").

questions.prompt: This sentence is correct: "While Tom was reading, his sister was watching TV."
questions.explanation: Two past actions happening at the same time can both be in the past continuous, often joined with "while".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "Sorry, I didn't hear you. I ___ to music on my headphones."
questions.explanation: Use the past continuous to describe what you were in the middle of doing when something else happened.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: "When I was arriving, they had lunch."
"When I arrived, they are having lunch."
"When I arrived, they were having lunch."
"When I arrive, they were having lunch."
questions.explanation: The short action ("arrived") is in the past simple and the action already in progress ("were having lunch") is in the past continuous.

questions.prompt: This sentence is correct: "When I was seeing the accident, I called the police."
questions.explanation: "See" is a short, completed action here and is not normally used in the continuous. Say "When I saw the accident, I called the police."

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "The sun ___ and the birds were singing when we woke up."
questions.explanation: Use the past continuous to describe the background scene of a story in the past.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "If it ___ tomorrow, we will stay at home."
questions.explanation: In the first conditional, use the present simple in the if-clause and "will" + verb in the main clause.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "If I ___ a million dollars, I would travel around the world."
questions.explanation: In the second conditional, use the past simple in the if-clause and "would" + verb in the main clause for imaginary situations.

questions.prompt: This sentence is correct: "If I will see Anna, I will tell her the news."
questions.explanation: Don't use "will" in the if-clause of a first conditional. The correct sentence is "If I see Anna, I will tell her the news."

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "If you don't hurry, you ___ the bus."
questions.explanation: This is a real, likely situation, so it is a first conditional: present simple in the if-clause, "will" + verb in the result.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "If I were you, I ___ to the doctor."
questions.explanation: "If I were you" is a second conditional used for advice, so the main clause needs "would" + verb.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "I ___ him your message if I see him at the party tonight."
questions.explanation: The if-clause is in the present simple ("see"), so this is a first conditional and the main clause needs "will" + verb.

questions.prompt: This sentence is correct: "If I were taller, I would play basketball."
questions.explanation: This is a correct second conditional about an imaginary present situation: past simple ("were") in the if-clause and "would" + verb in the result.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "What would you do if you ___ a snake in your bedroom?"
questions.explanation: The main clause uses "would", so this is a second conditional and the if-clause needs the past simple.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "___ you study harder, you won't pass the exam."
questions.explanation: "Unless" means "if not": "Unless you study harder" = "If you don't study harder".

questions.prompt: This sentence is correct: "If she had more free time, she will learn to play the guitar."
questions.explanation: A second conditional needs "would" in the main clause: "If she had more free time, she would learn to play the guitar."

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "The girl ___ sits next to me is from Brazil."
questions.explanation: Use "who" (or "that") to refer to people in a relative clause.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "That's the café ___ we first met."
questions.explanation: Use "where" to refer to a place when the relative clause has its own subject and verb ("we first met").

questions.prompt: This sentence is correct: "Mr Lee, that teaches us maths, is very kind."
questions.explanation: "That" cannot be used in a non-defining relative clause (one between commas). Use "who": "Mr Lee, who teaches us maths, is very kind."

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "I have a friend ___ father is a pilot."
questions.explanation: Use "whose" to show possession: "a friend whose father" = "a friend + his/her father".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "My phone, ___ I bought last month, has already stopped working."
questions.explanation: In a non-defining relative clause (with commas) about a thing, use "which", not "that".

questions.prompt: This sentence is correct: "The house where I grew up has been sold."
questions.explanation: "Where" correctly introduces a relative clause about a place ("the house").

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "The book ___ you lent me was really interesting."
questions.explanation: Use "that" or "which" for things in a defining relative clause; "what" cannot follow a noun like this.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
options: "My brother, who lives in London, is a doctor."
"My brother who lives in London, is a doctor."
"My brother, who lives in London is a doctor."
"My brother, that lives in London, is a doctor."
questions.explanation: A non-defining relative clause needs a comma at both the beginning and the end, and it cannot use "that".

questions.prompt: In which sentence can the relative pronoun be left out?
options: "The man who called you is my uncle."
"The film that we watched last night was scary."
"Paris, which is the capital of France, is beautiful."
"The dog that bit me ran away."
questions.explanation: You can leave out the relative pronoun in a defining clause only when it is the object of the verb ("we watched the film").

questions.prompt: This sentence is correct: "This is the student which won the prize."
questions.explanation: Use "who" or "that" for people, not "which": "This is the student who won the prize."

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "Could you ___ me a favour and carry this bag?"
questions.explanation: The fixed collocation is "do someone a favour".

questions.prompt: This sentence is correct: "I need to do my homework before dinner."
questions.explanation: We say "do homework", not "make homework". "Do" is used with tasks and work.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "We've ___ milk. Can you buy some on your way home?"
questions.explanation: "Run out of" something means to have none of it left.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "Please don't ___ so much noise. The baby is sleeping."
questions.explanation: The correct collocation is "make (a) noise".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "My dad ___ smoking last year, and now he feels much healthier."
questions.explanation: "Give up" (+ -ing) means to stop doing something, especially a habit.

questions.prompt: This sentence is correct: "She made her best to win the race."
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is "do your best", so it should be "She did her best to win the race."

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "It usually ___ me about 20 minutes to walk to school."
questions.explanation: Use "it takes (someone) + time + to do something" to talk about how long something lasts.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "Can you ___ my cat while I'm on holiday? It needs food twice a day."
questions.explanation: "Look after" means to take care of someone or something.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "I ___ a mistake in my homework, so the teacher asked me to correct it."
questions.explanation: We always say "make a mistake", never "do a mistake".

questions.prompt: In the sentence "I get on well with my cousins," the phrasal verb "get on with" means "to have a friendly relationship with".
questions.explanation: "Get on (well) with someone" means to like each other and have a good relationship.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "If I ___ how to fix computers, I would help you, but I don't."
questions.explanation: This is an imaginary present situation, so it needs the second conditional: past simple in the if-clause.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "The man ___ car was stolen called the police."
questions.explanation: "Whose" shows possession: the car belonged to the man.

questions.prompt: This sentence is correct: "The town where I was born has changed a lot since I left."
questions.explanation: "Where" correctly introduces a defining relative clause about a place.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "We ___ through the park when it started to rain, so we ran to a café."
questions.explanation: The longer action in progress uses the past continuous, and with "we" the auxiliary must be "were".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "I'll lend you my bike as long as you ___ careful with it."
questions.explanation: "As long as" works like "if" in a first conditional, so it is followed by the present simple, not "will".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "My grandmother, ___ is 85, still goes swimming every week."
questions.explanation: In a non-defining clause about a person, use "who"; "that" is not possible after a comma.

questions.prompt: This sentence is correct: "I was doing a lot of progress until I broke my arm."
questions.explanation: The collocation is "make progress", not "do progress": "I was making a lot of progress until I broke my arm."

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "I can't ___ all this noise any longer. I need some peace and quiet."
questions.explanation: "Put up with" means to accept or tolerate something unpleasant.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: "If I have a car, I would drive you to the station."
"If I had a car, I would drive you to the station."
"If I had a car, I will drive you to the station."
"If I would have a car, I would drive you to the station."
questions.explanation: A second conditional uses the past simple in the if-clause and "would" + verb in the main clause; never use "would" in the if-clause.

questions.prompt: This sentence is correct: "While I was waiting for the bus, I ran into an old friend from primary school."
questions.explanation: The past continuous shows the background action and the past simple shows the short event; "run into" means to meet someone by chance.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "The new bridge ___ by the end of next year."
questions.explanation: The future perfect passive (will have been + past participle) describes an action that will be finished before a future time; the bridge doesn't complete itself, so it must be passive.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "This form must ___ in black ink."
questions.explanation: A modal passive is formed with modal + be + past participle: "must be filled in".

questions.prompt: This sentence is correct: "I had my phone stolen on the bus yesterday."
questions.explanation: "Have something + past participle" can describe something bad that happened to you, caused by someone else.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "I can't use my laptop at the moment; it ___."
questions.explanation: The present continuous passive (is/are being + past participle) describes an action happening to something right now.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "We're ___ our kitchen redecorated next month."
questions.explanation: Use "have something done" when someone else does a job for you: "We're having our kitchen redecorated."

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "The suspect is believed ___ the country last week."
questions.explanation: After passive reporting verbs (is believed/said/thought), use the perfect infinitive "to have + past participle" for an earlier action.

questions.prompt: This sentence is correct: "The results have been announcing on the school website."
questions.explanation: The present perfect passive needs a past participle: "The results have been announced on the school website."

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "When we arrived at the hotel, our rooms ___, so we had to wait."
questions.explanation: The past continuous passive (was/were being + past participle) describes an action in progress at a past moment; rooms are cleaned by someone, so it must be passive.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "The documents ___ before the meeting, but nobody remembered to do it."
questions.explanation: "Should have been + past participle" is a perfect modal passive used to criticise something that was not done in the past.

questions.prompt: This sentence is correct: "It is said that the castle is haunted."
questions.explanation: "It is said that..." is a correct impersonal passive structure used to report what people generally say.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "If we had left earlier, we ___ the train."
questions.explanation: The third conditional describes an unreal past: if + past perfect, would have + past participle.

questions.prompt: This sentence is correct: "If I would have known you were ill, I would have visited you."
questions.explanation: Don't use "would have" in the if-clause. The correct form is "If I had known you were ill, I would have visited you."

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "If I ___ harder at school, I would have a better job now."
questions.explanation: This is a mixed conditional: a past condition (if + past perfect) with a present result (would + verb).

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "I wish I ___ so much cake last night. I feel sick."
questions.explanation: Use "wish + past perfect" to express regret about something that happened in the past.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "If only you ___ me the truth earlier!"
questions.explanation: "If only + past perfect" expresses a strong regret about the past, like "I wish".

questions.prompt: This sentence is correct: "If I hadn't missed the bus, I wouldn't be late for class now."
questions.explanation: This is a correct mixed conditional: a past condition (hadn't missed) with a present result (wouldn't be late now).

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "If she weren't so shy, she ___ to the party last night."
questions.explanation: This mixed conditional links a present situation (she is shy) to a past result: if + past simple, would have + past participle.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "I wish my neighbours ___ loud music every night. It's so annoying!"
questions.explanation: Use "wish + would/wouldn't" to complain about someone's annoying behaviour that you want to change.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "___ we known about the traffic, we would have taken the train."
questions.explanation: In formal English, "if" can be dropped in the third conditional by inverting "had" and the subject: "Had we known..." = "If we had known...".

questions.prompt: This sentence is correct: "I wish I can speak Japanese."
questions.explanation: For a present wish, use "wish + past form": "I wish I could speak Japanese."

questions.prompt: "Where do you live?" she asked. Choose the correct reported question: "She asked me where ___."
questions.explanation: Reported questions use normal statement word order (subject + verb) with no "do/did", and the tense usually moves back.

questions.prompt: This sentence is correct: "She asked me what time did the film start."
questions.explanation: Reported questions don't use question word order or "did". The correct sentence is "She asked me what time the film started."

questions.prompt: "Are you coming to the party?" Choose the correct reported question: "He asked me ___ to the party."
questions.explanation: Report yes/no questions with "if" or "whether" + subject + verb, not with "that" or question word order.

questions.prompt: "Don't touch the wire!" Choose the correct option: "The electrician ___ us not to touch the wire."
questions.explanation: "Warn someone (not) to do something" reports a warning about danger; "say" and "suggest" cannot be followed by an object + infinitive.

questions.prompt: "I didn't break the window," said Tom. Choose the correct option: "Tom denied ___ the window."
questions.explanation: "Deny" is followed by the -ing form (or "having" + past participle), not by an infinitive.

questions.prompt: "Let's go to the cinema," said Mia. Choose the correct option: "Mia suggested ___ to the cinema."
questions.explanation: "Suggest" is followed by the -ing form or a "that" clause, never by "to" + infinitive.

questions.prompt: This sentence is correct: "My mum told me to tidy my room before going out."
questions.explanation: Reported commands use "tell + object + to + infinitive".

questions.prompt: "Yes, I copied my friend's homework," said Leo. Choose the correct option: "Leo ___ copying his friend's homework."
questions.explanation: "Admit + -ing" reports that someone agreed they did something wrong.

questions.prompt: "Please close the door," the teacher said to me. Choose the correct option: "The teacher asked me ___ the door."
questions.explanation: Reported requests use "ask + object + to + infinitive".

questions.prompt: This sentence is correct: "He suggested me to take a taxi."
questions.explanation: "Suggest" cannot be followed by an object + infinitive. Say "He suggested (that) I take a taxi" or "He suggested taking a taxi."

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "___ the rain, we went for a walk."
questions.explanation: "Despite" is followed by a noun or -ing form; "although" and "whereas" need a full clause.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "The instructions were so ___ that nobody could understand them."
questions.explanation: Adjectives ending in -ing describe the thing that causes a feeling; -ed adjectives describe how people feel.

questions.prompt: This sentence is correct: "Despite of the heavy traffic, we arrived on time."
questions.explanation: "Despite" is never followed by "of". Use "Despite the heavy traffic" or "In spite of the heavy traffic".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "It's ___ to drive without a licence."
questions.explanation: Before words starting with "l", the negative prefix "in-" becomes "il-": legal → illegal.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "My brother loves sports, ___ I prefer reading."
questions.explanation: "Whereas" joins two clauses in one sentence to show a contrast between two people or things.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "The ___ of the new library took two years."
questions.explanation: After "the" and before "of", we need a noun; the suffix "-ion" turns the verb "construct" into a noun.

questions.prompt: The word "unbelievable" is formed with a negative prefix and an adjective suffix.
questions.explanation: "Unbelievable" = "un-" (negative prefix) + "believe" + "-able" (adjective suffix).

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "___ he was tired, he finished his homework."
questions.explanation: "Although" is followed by a full clause (subject + verb); "despite" and "in spite of" need a noun or -ing form.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "The service at the hotel was very good. ___, the rooms were small and noisy."
questions.explanation: "However" links two separate sentences to show contrast and is usually followed by a comma.

questions.prompt: The opposite of "patient" is "unpatient".
questions.explanation: The negative form of "patient" uses the prefix "im-": "impatient". "Im-" is often used before words starting with "p" or "m".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "If the email ___ to the wrong address, the client would have received it on time."
questions.explanation: This is a third conditional with a passive if-clause: if + had (not) been + past participle.

questions.prompt: This sentence is correct: "Had I known about the exam, I would have revised more."
questions.explanation: This is a correct inverted third conditional: "Had I known" = "If I had known".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "She apologised ___ late for the meeting."
questions.explanation: "Apologise" is followed by "for" + -ing form.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "___ having very little money, they always seemed happy."
questions.explanation: Only "despite" can be followed directly by an -ing form; "although" and "even though" need a full clause.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "The thief is thought ___ through the back window."
questions.explanation: After a passive reporting verb ("is thought"), use the perfect infinitive "to have + past participle" for an earlier action.

questions.prompt: This sentence is correct: "The manager denied to have lost the documents."
questions.explanation: "Deny" is followed by the -ing form: "The manager denied having lost (or losing) the documents."

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "I wish I ___ to my parents' advice when I chose my university course."
questions.explanation: To express regret about a past action, use "wish + past perfect".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "The coach ordered the players ___ late for training again."
questions.explanation: Negative reported commands use "order/tell + object + not to + infinitive".

questions.prompt: This sentence is correct: "Whereas her sister is outgoing, Lucy is quite shy."
questions.explanation: "Whereas" can start a sentence to introduce a contrasting clause, followed by a comma and the main clause.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: "Her ___ to help others makes her a great volunteer."
questions.explanation: After the possessive "her", we need a noun; the suffix "-ness" turns the adjective "willing" into the noun "willingness".

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "Not until the results came in ___ how close the race had been."
questions.explanation: After a fronted "Not until ..." clause, the main clause uses auxiliary inversion: "did we realise".

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "___ had I sat down than the phone rang."
questions.explanation: "No sooner" is paired with "than"; "Hardly", "Scarcely" and "Barely" are paired with "when".

questions.prompt: This sentence is grammatically correct: 'Seldom I have seen such dedication.'
questions.explanation: After a fronted negative adverb such as "Seldom", the subject and auxiliary must be inverted: "Seldom have I seen such dedication."

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "What I need ___ a long holiday."
questions.explanation: In a wh-cleft sentence the "What ..." clause is treated as singular, so with a singular complement the verb is "is".

questions.prompt: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
options: Under no circumstances you should leave the door unlocked.
Under no circumstances do you should leave the door unlocked.
Under no circumstances you leave should the door unlocked.
Under no circumstances should you leave the door unlocked.
questions.explanation: Fronted negative phrases like "Under no circumstances" require inversion of the modal and subject: "should you leave".

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "It was only when she read the letter ___ she understood what had happened."
questions.explanation: An "It was ... that" cleft sentence uses "that" to introduce the rest of the clause, even when the focus is a time expression.

questions.prompt: This sentence is grammatically correct: 'Little did he know that the police were already outside.'
questions.explanation: Fronted "Little" with a negative meaning triggers inversion with the auxiliary "did": "Little did he know".

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "So severe ___ that the match had to be abandoned."
questions.explanation: When "So + adjective" is fronted for emphasis, the verb "be" is inverted with the subject: "So severe was the storm that ...".

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "Only by working together ___ this problem."
questions.explanation: A fronted "Only by ..." phrase requires inversion in the main clause: auxiliary before subject, "will we solve".

questions.prompt: In the cleft sentence 'It was Tom who broke the window', the speaker is emphasising who broke the window.
questions.explanation: An "It was X who ..." cleft sentence puts the focus on X, here identifying Tom as the person responsible.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "The ground is soaking wet. It ___ rained heavily overnight."
questions.explanation: "Must have + past participle" expresses a confident deduction about the past based on present evidence.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "You ___ been at the party last night — I was there all evening and didn't see you."
questions.explanation: "Can't have + past participle" expresses certainty that something did not happen in the past.

questions.prompt: 'He might have missed the train' expresses certainty that he missed the train.
questions.explanation: "Might have" expresses only a possibility about the past; certainty would be expressed with "must have".

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "She ___ be at home — I can see her car in the drive and the lights are on."
questions.explanation: "Must + infinitive" expresses a confident deduction about the present based on evidence.

questions.prompt: Which sentence means "It is possible that he forgot about the meeting"?
options: He must have forgotten about the meeting.
He can't have forgotten about the meeting.
He may have forgotten about the meeting.
He should have forgotten about the meeting.
questions.explanation: "May have + past participle" expresses possibility about the past; "must have" is near certainty and "can't have" is impossibility.

questions.prompt: The modal in this sentence fits the evidence: 'They can't have gone out — the lights are off and the car has gone.'
questions.explanation: The evidence suggests they did go out, so the logical deduction is "They must have gone out".

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "I ___ left my keys at the restaurant; I definitely had them when I got into the taxi afterwards."
questions.explanation: Since the speaker definitely had the keys after leaving, it is impossible that they were left there: "can't have".

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "That ___ be Jack at the door — he's in Australia this week."
questions.explanation: "Can't + infinitive" expresses a logical impossibility in the present.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that correctly expresses a possibility about the past.
options: She could have taken the earlier bus.
She can have taken the earlier bus.
She must taken the earlier bus.
She might has taken the earlier bus.
questions.explanation: "Could have + past participle" expresses past possibility; "can have" is not used this way in affirmative statements.

questions.prompt: 'She must have been waiting for hours' uses the continuous form to make a deduction about an activity in progress over a period in the past.
questions.explanation: "Must have been + -ing" is used to deduce that an action was ongoing over a period in the past.

questions.prompt: Which word is the most formal equivalent of "find out"?
questions.explanation: "Ascertain" is a formal verb meaning to find out for certain; "suss out" and "dig up" are informal.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is most appropriate in a formal letter of complaint?
options: I'm really fed up with your service.
I wish to express my dissatisfaction with the service I received.
Your service is a total joke.
I'm gonna need you to sort this out.
questions.explanation: Formal complaints use impersonal, measured language such as "I wish to express my dissatisfaction", avoiding slang and emotive phrasing.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "Don't worry about the presentation — it'll be a piece of ___."
questions.explanation: "A piece of cake" is an informal idiom meaning something very easy.

questions.prompt: What does the idiom "to cut corners" mean?
options: to do something cheaply or carelessly to save time or money
to take a shorter route to save time
to reduce the number of staff
to avoid answering a question directly
questions.explanation: "To cut corners" means to do something in the easiest or cheapest way, often sacrificing quality.

questions.prompt: 'Commence' is a more formal alternative to 'start'.
questions.explanation: "Commence" belongs to a formal register and is typical of official or legal language, whereas "start" is neutral.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "She's been under the ___ all week, so she's staying at home."
questions.explanation: "Under the weather" is an informal idiom meaning slightly ill.

questions.prompt: Which is the most formal way to say "We need to look into this problem"?
options: We need to dig into this problem.
questions.explanation: Formal register favours nouns and impersonal structures ("requires investigation") over phrasal verbs and slang.

questions.prompt: 'To let the cat out of the bag' means to reveal a secret, usually by mistake.
questions.explanation: This informal idiom describes accidentally or carelessly disclosing something that was meant to be kept secret.

questions.prompt: What does "I'm all ears" mean?
options: I'm ready and eager to listen.
questions.explanation: "I'm all ears" is an informal way of saying you are listening attentively and want to hear more.

questions.prompt: 'Gonna' and 'wanna' are appropriate in a formal business report.
questions.explanation: "Gonna" and "wanna" are informal spoken forms; formal writing requires "going to" and "want to".

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "The new regulations will ___ small businesses most."
questions.explanation: "Affect" is the verb meaning to influence; "effect" is usually a noun (or a formal verb meaning to bring about).

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "From his tone, I ___ that he was unhappy with the decision."
questions.explanation: The listener "infers" (draws a conclusion); the speaker "implies" or "suggests" (hints at something).

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "The ___ interruptions from my neighbours' building work made it impossible to concentrate."
questions.explanation: "Continual" means repeated frequently with breaks in between; "continuous" means without any break at all.

questions.prompt: 'Principal' (main) and 'principle' (a fundamental rule) are interchangeable in writing.
questions.explanation: "Principal" means main or chief (or a head teacher), while "principle" means a basic truth or rule; they are not interchangeable.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "A judge must remain completely ___; she cannot favour either side."
questions.explanation: "Disinterested" means impartial, having nothing to gain; "uninterested" and "indifferent" mean not caring or bored.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "The signing of the peace treaty was a ___ moment for both nations."
questions.explanation: "Historic" means important or significant in history; "historical" means relating to the past or to the study of history.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "Buying in bulk is more ___ for large families."
questions.explanation: "Economical" means saving money or not wasteful; "economic" relates to the economy as a whole.

questions.prompt: 'Complement' means to praise someone, while 'compliment' means to complete or go well with something.
questions.explanation: The definitions are reversed: a "compliment" is praise, while to "complement" is to complete or go well with something.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "Let me ___ you that your data will be kept confidential."
questions.explanation: You "assure" a person (remove their doubts); you "ensure" that something happens and "insure" against financial loss.

questions.prompt: 'Imply' means to suggest something indirectly, while 'infer' means to draw a conclusion from evidence.
questions.explanation: The speaker or writer implies; the listener or reader infers.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "___ he arrived on time, he would have been able to meet the director."
questions.explanation: An inverted third conditional uses "Had + subject + past participle" in place of "If he had arrived".

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "Rarely ___ such a compelling argument presented with so little evidence."
questions.explanation: Fronted "Rarely" requires auxiliary inversion; in the present simple, "does" is added: "does one hear".

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "He looks utterly exhausted. He ___ up all night finishing the report."
questions.explanation: Present evidence (he looks exhausted) supports a confident deduction about the past: "must have been".

questions.prompt: This sentence is grammatically correct: 'It's not the money that worries me but the time it will take.'
questions.explanation: This is a well-formed "It is not X that ... but Y" cleft sentence contrasting two focused elements.

questions.prompt: In a formal report, which phrase best replaces "a lot of" in "a lot of respondents"?
questions.explanation: "A considerable number of" is formal and used with countable nouns; "loads/tons/heaps of" are informal.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "The minister's statement ___ that cuts were imminent, though she never said so directly."
questions.explanation: A statement or speaker "implies" (hints); "infer", "deduce" and "conclude" describe what the listener does.

questions.prompt: 'She can't have finished already' expresses the speaker's near certainty that she has NOT finished.
questions.explanation: "Can't have + past participle" signals that the speaker believes something is impossible or very unlikely.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "Not only ___ the deadline, but they also went over budget."
questions.explanation: A fronted "Not only" requires auxiliary inversion; with a past simple verb, "did" is used: "did they miss".

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "After weeks of arguing, the two brothers finally decided to bury the ___."
questions.explanation: "Bury the hatchet" is a fixed idiom meaning to end a quarrel and become friendly again.

questions.prompt: This sentence is grammatically correct: 'Hardly had she left the room than the argument started again.'
questions.explanation: "Hardly" is paired with "when", not "than": "Hardly had she left the room when the argument started again."

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "Given the latest polls, the outcome of the election was a ___ conclusion."
questions.explanation: "A foregone conclusion" is a fixed collocation meaning a result that is certain before it happens.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "Rising sea levels ___ a serious threat to coastal communities."
questions.explanation: "Pose a threat" is the standard collocation; "make", "give" and "do" do not combine with "threat" in this sense.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "Low-income households will ___ the brunt of the tax increase."
questions.explanation: "Bear the brunt of" is a fixed collocation meaning to suffer the worst part of something.

questions.prompt: 'Make a decision' and 'take a decision' are both acceptable collocations in British English.
questions.explanation: "Make a decision" is universal, and "take a decision" is also standard in British English.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "Her remarks during the interview ___ a storm of controversy."
questions.explanation: "Unleash a storm (of controversy/criticism)" is a natural collocation; the other verbs do not collocate with "storm" in this sense.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "The company's reputation suffered ___ damage after the scandal."
questions.explanation: "Irreparable damage" is the fixed collocation for harm that cannot be put right.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "The plan was ___ with difficulties from the very start."
questions.explanation: "Fraught with" (difficulty, danger, tension) means full of something undesirable; the other adjectives do not take "with" in this sense.

questions.prompt: 'Heavy rain' and 'strong rain' are equally natural collocations in English.
questions.explanation: English uses "heavy rain"; "strong" collocates with "wind", not "rain".

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "Despite repeated warnings, the authorities ___ a blind eye to the problem."
questions.explanation: "Turn a blind eye to" is a fixed expression meaning to deliberately ignore something.

questions.prompt: 'Commit a crime' and 'perform a crime' are equally acceptable collocations.
questions.explanation: The natural collocation is "commit a crime"; "perform" does not collocate with "crime".

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "Her latest lie was the ___ that broke the camel's back."
questions.explanation: "The straw that broke the camel's back" is the final small problem that makes a situation unbearable.

questions.prompt: What does "to be on tenterhooks" mean?
options: to be trapped in a difficult situation
to be anxious and in suspense
questions.explanation: "On tenterhooks" describes nervous suspense while waiting for news or an outcome.

questions.prompt: The phrase "a double-edged sword" describes something that:
options: has both favourable and unfavourable consequences
questions.explanation: A double-edged sword is something whose benefits come with corresponding drawbacks.

questions.prompt: 'To throw the baby out with the bathwater' means to discard something valuable while getting rid of something unwanted.
questions.explanation: The idiom warns against rejecting the good parts of something along with the bad.

questions.prompt: "Our office is a well-oiled machine." This metaphor suggests the office:
questions.explanation: A "well-oiled machine" figuratively describes an organisation that runs smoothly with no friction.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "The CEO's resignation came out of the ___; nobody had seen it coming."
questions.explanation: "Out of the blue" means completely unexpectedly.

questions.prompt: What does "to damn with faint praise" mean?
options: to criticise indirectly by giving only lukewarm approval
to praise someone behind their back
questions.explanation: Praising something only half-heartedly can signal disapproval more effectively than open criticism.

questions.prompt: 'To have a chip on your shoulder' means to be in a cheerful and optimistic mood.
questions.explanation: Having a chip on your shoulder means harbouring a long-standing grievance or feeling resentful.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "He's been resting on his ___ since winning the award and hasn't produced anything new."
questions.explanation: "Rest on one's laurels" means to rely on past achievements instead of making further effort.

questions.prompt: 'A Pyrrhic victory' is a victory gained at such great cost that it is hardly worth winning.
questions.explanation: Named after King Pyrrhus, whose victories over Rome cost him most of his army.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "The committee recommended that the proposal ___ rejected."
questions.explanation: Verbs of recommendation take the mandative subjunctive: "that + subject + base form" ("be rejected").

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "___ it not been for your timely intervention, the project would have collapsed."
questions.explanation: "Had it not been for" is the inverted form of "If it had not been for" in a third conditional.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "Will it rain tomorrow?" — "I hope ___."
questions.explanation: With "hope", the negative substitute for a clause is "not" ("I hope not"), never "I don't hope so" or "I hope not so".

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "___ the report, she realised that several figures were missing."
questions.explanation: A perfect participle clause ("Having read") shows an action completed by the subject before the main action.

questions.prompt: This sentence contains a dangling participle: 'Walking down the street, the trees looked beautiful.'
questions.explanation: The implied subject of "walking" is a person, but the main clause subject is "the trees", so the participle dangles.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "___ by the scale of the task, the volunteers nonetheless refused to give up."
questions.explanation: A past participle clause ("Daunted") has a passive meaning: the volunteers were daunted by the task.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "I'd have gone to the concert if I could ___."
questions.explanation: In ellipsis after a modal perfect, the main verb is dropped but "have" is retained: "if I could have (gone)".

questions.prompt: In 'If need be, we can work over the weekend', 'be' is an example of a fixed subjunctive expression.
questions.explanation: "If need be" preserves the old subjunctive form "be", like "so be it" and "be that as it may".

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "Far ___ it from me to criticise, but your essay needs more work."
questions.explanation: "Far be it from me" is a fixed expression that uses the subjunctive "be".

questions.prompt: This sentence is grammatically correct: 'Being a rainy day, we decided to stay at home.'
questions.explanation: The participle clause wrongly refers to "we"; the correct form uses an absolute clause: "It being a rainy day, ...".

questions.prompt: "Oh, wonderful — another meeting that could have been an email," she sighed. What is the speaker's tone?
questions.explanation: The positive word "wonderful" combined with "sighed" and the complaint signals sarcasm.

questions.prompt: "While the proposal is not without merit, it would benefit from considerably more rigour." The writer's attitude to the proposal is best described as:
questions.explanation: "Not without merit" concedes some value, while "would benefit from considerably more rigour" politely signals serious reservations.

questions.prompt: "The hotel's 'sea view' required a certain amount of imagination and a good pair of binoculars." What does the writer imply?
options: The hotel provided binoculars for guests.
The hotel was right on the beach.
The sea was barely visible from the hotel.
questions.explanation: The ironic reference to imagination and binoculars implies the advertised view was misleading.

questions.prompt: In the sentence 'He is, shall we say, economical with the truth', the writer is suggesting that he is dishonest.
questions.explanation: "Economical with the truth" is a euphemism for lying, and "shall we say" signals deliberate understatement.

questions.prompt: "Needless to say, the minister's promise to cut waiting times proved about as durable as a snowflake in July." The writer's attitude towards the minister is:
questions.explanation: The absurd simile ridicules the promise as short-lived, and "Needless to say" implies it was predictable.

questions.prompt: "It is not unreasonable to suggest that the policy has had some unintended consequences." The use of "not unreasonable" and "some" makes the claim:
questions.explanation: Litotes ("not unreasonable") and the vague quantifier "some" soften the claim, a typical hedging strategy in academic writing.

questions.prompt: "I'd love to stay and chat, but I wouldn't want to keep you from your important work," he said, glancing at the clock. What is most likely implied?
options: He greatly admires the listener's work.
He wants to end the conversation.
He has nothing else to do.
He is worried about the listener's workload.
questions.explanation: The polite excuse plus the glance at the clock implies he is looking for a tactful way to leave.

questions.prompt: In the extract 'Her performance was, to put it kindly, adequate', the writer is expressing high praise.
questions.explanation: "To put it kindly" signals that "adequate" is a generous description of a disappointing performance.

questions.prompt: "Having waited ninety minutes for a table, we were finally rewarded with lukewarm soup and a waiter who regarded us as an inconvenience." The tone of this review is:
questions.explanation: The word "rewarded" is used ironically, since the experience described is clearly negative.

questions.prompt: The phrase 'with the greatest respect' in 'With the greatest respect, Minister, that is simply not the case' usually signals strong agreement.
questions.explanation: In formal debate, "with the greatest respect" typically introduces firm disagreement, softened by politeness.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "The scandal dealt a severe ___ to the party's chances of re-election."
questions.explanation: "Deal a blow to" is a fixed collocation meaning to cause serious damage or disappointment.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "His argument doesn't hold ___ under close scrutiny."
questions.explanation: An argument that "doesn't hold water" is unconvincing because it does not stand up to examination.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "It is imperative that the patient ___ informed of the risks before surgery."
questions.explanation: After "It is imperative that", the mandative subjunctive uses the base form: "the patient be informed".

questions.prompt: 'Not that I'm complaining, but the room is rather cold' — here the speaker is, in fact, complaining.
questions.explanation: "Not that I'm complaining, but ..." is a hedge that typically introduces exactly the complaint it denies.

questions.prompt: "The report, all 400 pages of it, manages to say remarkably little." The writer suggests the report is:
questions.explanation: The contrast between "all 400 pages" and "remarkably little" ironically criticises the report's lack of content.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "___ in a hurry, the letter contained several errors."
questions.explanation: The letter was written by someone, so a passive past participle clause ("Written") correctly refers to the subject "the letter".

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: "The new evidence ___ serious doubt on his version of events."
questions.explanation: "Cast doubt on" is the standard collocation for making something seem less certain or true.

questions.prompt: This sentence is grammatically correct: 'Should you require further assistance, please do not hesitate to contact us.'
questions.explanation: Inverted "Should you require" is a formal alternative to "If you require" in conditional clauses.

questions.prompt: What does "to move the goalposts" mean?
options: to change the rules or targets unfairly once a process has begun
to achieve a goal ahead of schedule
to switch to a different team
questions.explanation: The idiom describes unfairly altering conditions so that success becomes harder to achieve.

questions.prompt: Describing a proposal as receiving 'lukewarm support' implies enthusiastic and wholehearted backing.
questions.explanation: "Lukewarm support" figuratively means half-hearted or unenthusiastic approval.

questions.prompt: Bạn hỏi « Where are you from? », em trả lời thế nào?
questions.explanation: « Where are you from? » hỏi em đến từ đâu, nên em trả lời « I'm from Viet Nam. » (Mình đến từ Việt Nam).

questions.prompt: « Người Việt Nam » (quốc tịch Việt Nam) trong tiếng Anh là gì?
questions.explanation: Quốc tịch Việt Nam là « Vietnamese », còn « Viet Nam » là tên đất nước nhé em.

questions.prompt: Câu hỏi « What's your address? » dùng để hỏi địa chỉ của bạn.
questions.explanation: Đúng rồi! « Address » nghĩa là địa chỉ, nên câu này hỏi bạn sống ở đâu.

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: Akiko is from Japan. She is ___.
questions.explanation: Bạn ấy đến từ Nhật Bản (Japan) nên quốc tịch là « Japanese » (người Nhật).

questions.prompt: Bạn hỏi « How old are you? », Mai trả lời thế nào?
questions.explanation: « How old are you? » là hỏi tuổi, nên Mai trả lời « I'm eleven years old. » (Mình 11 tuổi).

questions.prompt: Câu « I'm from England. I'm English. » là câu đúng.
questions.explanation: Chính xác! Đất nước là « England » (nước Anh), còn quốc tịch là « English » (người Anh).

questions.prompt: Chọn câu hỏi phù hợp với câu trả lời: « I live at 25 Tran Phu Street. »
questions.explanation: Câu trả lời nói về nơi ở (số nhà, tên phố), nên câu hỏi là « Where do you live? » (Bạn sống ở đâu?).

questions.prompt: « Nationality » nghĩa là gì?
questions.explanation: « Nationality » nghĩa là quốc tịch, ví dụ: « My nationality is Vietnamese. »

questions.prompt: Câu « What's you name? » là câu hỏi đúng.
questions.explanation: Câu này sai rồi em ơi! Phải dùng « your » (của bạn): « What's your name? »

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: ___ is your best friend? – It's Nam.
questions.explanation: Hỏi về một người thì dùng « Who » (Ai): « Who is your best friend? » – Bạn thân của em là ai?

questions.prompt: « Môn Toán » trong tiếng Anh là gì?
questions.explanation: Môn Toán là « Maths ». Science là Khoa học, Music là Âm nhạc, Art là Mĩ thuật.

questions.prompt: « Science » là môn học nào?
questions.explanation: « Science » là môn Khoa học, nơi em tìm hiểu về cây cối, con vật và thế giới tự nhiên.

questions.prompt: « IT » là tên tiếng Anh của môn Tin học.
questions.explanation: Đúng rồi! « IT » (Information Technology) là môn Tin học, em được học về máy tính đó.

questions.prompt: Bạn hỏi « What subjects do you have today? », em trả lời thế nào?
options: I go to school by bike.
questions.explanation: Câu hỏi muốn biết hôm nay em học môn gì, nên trả lời « I have Maths and English. »

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: I have English ___ Mondays and Wednesdays.
questions.explanation: Trước các ngày trong tuần, em dùng giới từ « on »: on Mondays, on Wednesdays.

questions.prompt: « PE » là tên tiếng Anh của môn Âm nhạc.
questions.explanation: « PE » là môn Thể dục (Physical Education). Môn Âm nhạc là « Music » nhé em.

questions.prompt: Bạn hỏi « How often do you have Art? », em trả lời thế nào?
questions.explanation: « How often » hỏi bao lâu một lần, nên em trả lời « Twice a week. » (Hai lần một tuần).

questions.prompt: Chọn từ khác loại:
questions.explanation: « Teacher » là giáo viên (chỉ người), còn Maths, History, Geography đều là tên môn học.

questions.prompt: « Timetable » nghĩa là thời khóa biểu.
questions.explanation: Chính xác! Nhìn vào « timetable » là em biết mỗi ngày học những môn gì.

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: What's your favourite ___? – It's English.
questions.explanation: Câu trả lời là « English » (một môn học), nên câu hỏi là « What's your favourite subject? »

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: She ___ up at six o'clock every morning.
questions.explanation: Chủ ngữ « She » ở thì hiện tại đơn thì động từ thêm « s »: she gets up.

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: My brother ___ his teeth after breakfast.
questions.explanation: Động từ tận cùng bằng « sh » thì thêm « es » khi đi với he/she: brushes.

questions.prompt: Câu « He watchs TV in the evening. » là câu đúng.
questions.explanation: Động từ tận cùng bằng « ch » phải thêm « es »: « He watches TV in the evening. »

questions.prompt: « Always » nghĩa là gì?
questions.explanation: « Always » nghĩa là luôn luôn. Thỉnh thoảng là « sometimes », không bao giờ là « never ».

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: I ___ do my homework after dinner. (thường thường)
questions.explanation: « Usually » nghĩa là thường thường, đúng với gợi ý trong ngoặc của câu.

questions.prompt: « Never » nghĩa là không bao giờ.
questions.explanation: Đúng rồi! Ví dụ: « I never go to bed late. » – Em không bao giờ đi ngủ muộn.

questions.prompt: Chọn câu đúng:
options: Mai go to school by bike.
Mai goes to school by bike.
Mai going to school by bike.
Mai gos to school by bike.
questions.explanation: « Mai » là một người (như « she »), động từ « go » thêm « es » thành « goes ».

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: ___ your father cook dinner? – Yes, he does.
questions.explanation: Hỏi về « your father » (như « he ») ở thì hiện tại đơn thì dùng « Does ».

questions.prompt: Trong câu « I always get up early. », trạng từ « always » đứng trước động từ thường « get ».
questions.explanation: Chính xác! Trạng từ chỉ tần suất như always, usually thường đứng trước động từ thường.

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: Nam ___ like milk.
questions.explanation: « Nam » là ngôi thứ ba số ít nên câu phủ định dùng « doesn't »: Nam doesn't like milk.

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: I ___ at home yesterday.
questions.explanation: Có « yesterday » nên dùng thì quá khứ, và « I » đi với « was ».

questions.prompt: Câu « They was at the zoo last Sunday. » là câu đúng.
questions.explanation: « They » ở quá khứ phải đi với « were »: « They were at the zoo last Sunday. »

questions.prompt: Dạng quá khứ của « play » là gì?
questions.explanation: « Play » có nguyên âm trước « y » nên chỉ cần thêm « ed »: played.

questions.prompt: Dạng quá khứ của « go » là gì?
questions.explanation: « Go » là động từ bất quy tắc, quá khứ của nó là « went », em nhớ học thuộc nhé.

questions.prompt: Bạn hỏi « What did you do yesterday? », em trả lời thế nào?
questions.explanation: Câu hỏi về hôm qua nên em trả lời bằng thì quá khứ: « I watched TV. »

questions.prompt: Dạng quá khứ của « study » là « studied ».
questions.explanation: Đúng rồi! Động từ tận cùng bằng phụ âm + « y » thì đổi « y » thành « i » rồi thêm « ed ».

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: ___ you at school yesterday? – Yes, I was.
questions.explanation: Câu hỏi với « you » ở quá khứ dùng « Were »: Were you at school yesterday?

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: She ___ her grandparents last weekend.
questions.explanation: « Last weekend » là dấu hiệu quá khứ, nên « visit » thêm « ed » thành « visited ».

questions.prompt: « Yesterday » nghĩa là ngày mai.
questions.explanation: « Yesterday » là hôm qua. Ngày mai là « tomorrow » nhé em.

questions.prompt: Chọn câu hỏi đúng:
options: Did you go to the park?
Did you went to the park?
Do you went to the park?
Did you going to the park?
questions.explanation: Sau « Did » dùng động từ nguyên mẫu, nên câu đúng là « Did you go to the park? »

questions.prompt: Bạn hỏi « Where do you live? », em trả lời thế nào?
options: I live at 12 Le Loi Street.
questions.explanation: « Where do you live? » hỏi nơi ở, nên em trả lời bằng địa chỉ: « I live at 12 Le Loi Street. »

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: Linda ___ Music on Tuesdays and Fridays.
questions.explanation: « Linda » là ngôi thứ ba số ít nên dùng « has »: Linda has Music on Tuesdays and Fridays.

questions.prompt: Câu « Yesterday Tom goes to the library. » là câu đúng.
questions.explanation: Có « yesterday » nên phải dùng quá khứ: « Yesterday Tom went to the library. »

questions.prompt: Chọn đáp án đúng: My sister usually ___ to bed at nine, but last night she ___ to bed at eleven.
questions.explanation: « Usually » là thói quen nên dùng « goes »; « last night » là quá khứ nên dùng « went ».

questions.prompt: « Geography » là môn học nào?
questions.explanation: « Geography » là môn Địa lí, nơi em học về bản đồ, núi sông và các nước. Lịch sử là « History ».

questions.prompt: « Where are you from? – I'm from Australia. » là một cặp hỏi đáp đúng.
questions.explanation: Đúng rồi! Hỏi em đến từ đâu thì trả lời « I'm from + tên đất nước ».

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: We ___ very tired after the long trip yesterday.
questions.explanation: Có « yesterday » nên dùng quá khứ, và « We » đi với « were ».

questions.prompt: Tìm từ sai trong câu « She always walk to school. »
questions.explanation: Chủ ngữ « She » ở thì hiện tại đơn nên « walk » phải thêm « s »: She always walks to school.

questions.prompt: Câu « Do he play badminton after school? » là câu đúng.
questions.explanation: Với « he » phải dùng « Does »: « Does he play badminton after school? »

questions.prompt: Sắp xếp thành câu đúng: did / What / do / you / yesterday
questions.explanation: Câu hỏi quá khứ có dạng: Từ để hỏi + did + chủ ngữ + động từ nguyên mẫu, nên là « What did you do yesterday? »

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: Look! The children ___ in the garden.
questions.explanation: « Look! » cho thấy việc đang diễn ra ngay lúc này, nên dùng hiện tại tiếp diễn: are playing.

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: My mum ___ dinner now.
questions.explanation: Có « now » (bây giờ) nên dùng hiện tại tiếp diễn; « My mum » đi với « is »: is cooking.

questions.prompt: Câu « She is reading a book at the moment. » là câu đúng.
questions.explanation: Đúng rồi! « At the moment » là dấu hiệu hiện tại tiếp diễn, và « She » đi với « is reading ».

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: Lan ___ to school by bus every day.
questions.explanation: « Every day » chỉ thói quen nên dùng hiện tại đơn; « Lan » là ngôi thứ ba số ít nên là « goes ».

questions.prompt: Dạng V-ing của « swim » là gì?
questions.explanation: « Swim » có một nguyên âm kẹp giữa hai phụ âm ở cuối, nên gấp đôi « m » rồi thêm « ing »: swimming.

questions.prompt: Câu « I am liking ice cream very much. » là câu đúng.
questions.explanation: « Like » là động từ chỉ cảm xúc, thường không dùng ở thì tiếp diễn. Câu đúng là « I like ice cream very much. »

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: What ___ you doing now? – I'm doing my homework.
questions.explanation: Câu hỏi hiện tại tiếp diễn với « you » dùng « are »: What are you doing now?

questions.prompt: Cụm từ nào là dấu hiệu của thì hiện tại tiếp diễn?
questions.explanation: « At the moment » (ngay lúc này) báo hiệu hành động đang xảy ra. Các cụm còn lại chỉ thói quen.

questions.prompt: Dạng V-ing của « write » là « writing ».
questions.explanation: Chính xác! Động từ tận cùng bằng « e » câm thì bỏ « e » rồi thêm « ing »: writing.

questions.prompt: Chọn đáp án đúng: He usually ___ jeans, but today he ___ a uniform.
questions.explanation: « Usually » là thói quen nên dùng « wears »; « today » nói về việc đang diễn ra nên dùng « is wearing ».

questions.prompt: Dạng so sánh hơn của « tall » là gì?
questions.explanation: « Tall » là tính từ ngắn nên chỉ cần thêm « er »: taller (cao hơn).

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: An elephant is ___ than a horse.
questions.explanation: « Big » kết thúc bằng phụ âm–nguyên âm–phụ âm nên gấp đôi « g »: bigger than.

questions.prompt: Dạng so sánh nhất của « good » là « goodest ».
questions.explanation: « Good » là tính từ bất quy tắc: good – better – best. Vậy so sánh nhất là « the best ».

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: This book is ___ than that one. (thú vị hơn)
questions.explanation: « Interesting » là tính từ dài nên so sánh hơn dùng « more »: more interesting than.

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: Ha Noi is one of the ___ cities in Viet Nam.
questions.explanation: Sau « one of the » ta dùng so sánh nhất: one of the biggest cities (một trong những thành phố lớn nhất).

questions.prompt: Dạng so sánh hơn của « happy » là « happier ».
questions.explanation: Đúng rồi! Tính từ tận cùng bằng « y » thì đổi « y » thành « i » rồi thêm « er »: happier.

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: My handwriting is bad, but Tom's handwriting is ___.
questions.explanation: « Bad » là tính từ bất quy tắc: bad – worse – worst. Ở đây so sánh hai người nên dùng « worse ».

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: Who is ___ student in your class?
questions.explanation: So sánh một bạn với cả lớp thì dùng so sánh nhất, và nhớ có « the »: the tallest.

questions.prompt: Câu « Summer is hotter than winter. » đúng ngữ pháp.
questions.explanation: Chính xác! « Hot » gấp đôi « t » rồi thêm « er »: hotter than.

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: Of the three girls, Lan is ___ beautiful.
questions.explanation: So sánh trong một nhóm ba người trở lên dùng so sánh nhất; « beautiful » là tính từ dài nên dùng « the most ».

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: There ___ a sofa in the living room.
questions.explanation: « A sofa » là một vật (số ít) nên dùng « There is ».

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: There ___ two lamps on the table.
questions.explanation: « Two lamps » là số nhiều nên dùng « There are ».

questions.prompt: « Next to » nghĩa là bên cạnh.
questions.explanation: Đúng rồi! Ví dụ: « The bed is next to the window. » – Cái giường ở bên cạnh cửa sổ.

questions.prompt: « Bathroom » là phòng nào?
questions.explanation: « Bathroom » là phòng tắm. Phòng ngủ là « bedroom », phòng khách là « living room », nhà bếp là « kitchen ».

questions.prompt: Con mèo nằm ở giữa cái ghế và cái bàn. Chọn câu đúng:
options: The cat is behind the chair and the table.
The cat is under the chair and the table.
The cat is next the chair and the table.
The cat is between the chair and the table.
questions.explanation: « Between ... and ... » nghĩa là ở giữa hai vật, đúng với vị trí của con mèo.

questions.prompt: « Behind » nghĩa là ở phía trước.
questions.explanation: « Behind » là ở phía sau. Ở phía trước là « in front of » nhé em.

questions.prompt: Nhà em thường nấu ăn ở phòng nào?
questions.explanation: « Kitchen » là nhà bếp, nơi cả nhà nấu ăn hằng ngày.

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: The dog is sleeping ___ the bed. (ở dưới)
questions.explanation: « Under » nghĩa là ở dưới, nên chú chó đang ngủ dưới gầm giường: under the bed.

questions.prompt: « Is there a fridge in your kitchen? – Yes, there are. » là một cặp hỏi đáp đúng.
questions.explanation: Hỏi bằng « Is there » thì trả lời « Yes, there is. » vì « a fridge » là số ít.

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: ___ there any chairs in the room?
questions.explanation: « Any chairs » là số nhiều nên câu hỏi dùng « Are there ».

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: I think it ___ rain tomorrow.
questions.explanation: « I think » là đoán về tương lai, nên dùng « will » + động từ nguyên mẫu: will rain.

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: Look at those dark clouds! It is ___ rain.
questions.explanation: Thấy mây đen là có dấu hiệu sắp mưa, nên dùng « be going to »: It is going to rain.

questions.prompt: Câu « She will goes to the cinema tomorrow. » là câu đúng.
questions.explanation: Sau « will » luôn dùng động từ nguyên mẫu: « She will go to the cinema tomorrow. »

questions.prompt: Cụm từ nào chỉ thời gian trong tương lai?
questions.explanation: « Next week » nghĩa là tuần sau, nói về tương lai. Các cụm còn lại đều chỉ quá khứ.

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: My parents ___ going to buy a new car.
questions.explanation: « My parents » là số nhiều (như « they ») nên đi với « are »: are going to buy.

questions.prompt: Câu « I'm going to visit Hue next summer. » nói về một kế hoạch em đã dự định trước.
questions.explanation: Đúng rồi! « Be going to » thường dùng để nói về kế hoạch, dự định đã có từ trước.

questions.prompt: Chọn câu phủ định đúng:
options: I don't will be late tomorrow.
I will not to be late tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Phủ định của « will » là « will not », viết tắt là « won't »: I won't be late tomorrow.

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: ___ you help me with my homework tonight? – Sure, I will.
questions.explanation: Câu trả lời là « I will », nên câu hỏi bắt đầu bằng « Will »: Will you help me ...?

questions.prompt: « Tomorrow » nghĩa là ngày mai.
questions.explanation: Chính xác! « See you tomorrow! » nghĩa là « Hẹn gặp lại ngày mai! »

questions.prompt: Bạn hỏi « What are you going to do this weekend? », em trả lời thế nào?
options: I went camping with my family.
I'm going to go camping with my family.
questions.explanation: Câu hỏi dùng « be going to » về kế hoạch cuối tuần này, nên em trả lời « I'm going to go camping ... ».

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: Be quiet! The baby ___.
questions.explanation: « Be quiet! » cho thấy em bé đang ngủ ngay lúc này, nên dùng hiện tại tiếp diễn: is sleeping.

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: Mount Everest is ___ mountain in the world.
questions.explanation: So sánh với tất cả các ngọn núi trên thế giới nên dùng so sánh nhất có « the »: the highest.

questions.prompt: Câu « There are a big garden behind my house. » là câu đúng.
questions.explanation: « A big garden » là số ít nên phải dùng « There is a big garden behind my house. »

questions.prompt: Chọn câu đúng:
options: My house is bigger than yours.
My house is more big than yours.
My house is biggest than yours.
My house is the bigger than yours.
questions.explanation: « Big » là tính từ ngắn nên so sánh hơn là « bigger than », không dùng « more ».

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: Next year, my brother ___ 15 years old.
questions.explanation: « Next year » là tương lai nên dùng « will be »: Next year, my brother will be 15.

questions.prompt: « What are you doing now? – I watch TV. » là một cặp hỏi đáp đúng.
questions.explanation: Câu hỏi ở hiện tại tiếp diễn nên phải trả lời « I'm watching TV. »

questions.prompt: Tìm phần sai trong câu « There is a lamp between the bed or the desk. »
questions.explanation: Cấu trúc đúng là « between ... and ... », nên phải sửa « or » thành « and ».

questions.prompt: Chọn đáp án đúng: My sister ___ her homework every evening, but tonight she ___ a film.
questions.explanation: « Every evening » là thói quen nên dùng « does »; « tonight » nói về việc đang diễn ra nên dùng « is watching ».

questions.prompt: Câu « This is the best day of my life! » dùng đúng dạng so sánh nhất của « good ».
questions.explanation: Đúng rồi! good – better – best, nên so sánh nhất là « the best ».

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: We have bought the tickets. We ___ fly to Da Nang next Friday.
questions.explanation: Đã mua vé là đã có kế hoạch, nên dùng « be going to »: We are going to fly ... Các đáp án khác sai ngữ pháp.

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: « She ___ to school by bus yesterday. »
questions.explanation: Có « yesterday » nên em dùng thì quá khứ đơn. « Go » là động từ bất quy tắc, quá khứ của nó là « went ».

questions.prompt: Dạng quá khứ của « buy » là gì?
questions.explanation: « Buy » → « bought ». Em đừng nhầm với « brought », là quá khứ của « bring » nhé.

questions.prompt: Dạng quá khứ của « eat » là « ate ».
questions.explanation: Đúng rồi! « Eat » là động từ bất quy tắc: eat → ate.

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: « ___ you watch the football match last night? »
questions.explanation: Câu hỏi quá khứ đơn với động từ thường có dạng « Did + chủ ngữ + động từ nguyên mẫu? ».

questions.prompt: Chọn câu đúng:
questions.explanation: Câu phủ định quá khứ đơn là « didn't + động từ nguyên mẫu », nên « see » giữ nguyên, không đổi thành « saw ».

questions.prompt: Câu « He didn't went to the party. » là câu đúng.
questions.explanation: Sau « didn't » em phải dùng động từ nguyên mẫu. Câu đúng là « He didn't go to the party. »

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: « Last summer, my family ___ a trip to Ha Long Bay. »
questions.explanation: « Last summer » báo hiệu thì quá khứ đơn. Quá khứ bất quy tắc của « take » là « took ».

questions.prompt: Dạng quá khứ đơn của « write » là gì?
questions.explanation: « Write » → « wrote ». Còn « written » là quá khứ phân từ (V3), dùng cho thì hoàn thành em nhé.

questions.prompt: « Did Nam have breakfast this morning? » – Nam đã ăn rồi. Câu trả lời đúng là:
questions.explanation: Câu hỏi bắt đầu bằng « Did » thì câu trả lời ngắn cũng dùng « did »: Yes, he did.

questions.prompt: Dạng quá khứ của « think » là « thought ».
questions.explanation: Chính xác! « Think » là động từ bất quy tắc: think → thought.

questions.prompt: Danh từ nào KHÔNG đếm được?
questions.explanation: « Rice » (gạo, cơm) là danh từ không đếm được, ta không nói « two rices ». Các từ còn lại đều đếm được.

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: « How ___ milk do you drink every day? »
questions.explanation: « Milk » là danh từ không đếm được nên em hỏi số lượng bằng « How much ».

questions.prompt: « Bread » là danh từ đếm được nên ta có thể nói « two breads ».
questions.explanation: « Bread » không đếm được. Em nói « two loaves of bread » hoặc « two pieces of bread » nhé.

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: « There aren't ___ eggs in the fridge. »
questions.explanation: Trong câu phủ định em dùng « any ». « Much » chỉ đi với danh từ không đếm được, còn « eggs » đếm được.

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: « How ___ students are there in your class? »
questions.explanation: « Students » là danh từ đếm được số nhiều, nên em hỏi số lượng bằng « How many ».

questions.prompt: « A lot of » dùng được với cả danh từ đếm được và danh từ không đếm được.
questions.explanation: Đúng rồi! Ví dụ: « a lot of books » (đếm được) và « a lot of water » (không đếm được).

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: « I'd like ___ water, please. »
questions.explanation: « Water » không đếm được nên không dùng « a/an » hay « many ». Trong lời đề nghị lịch sự, em dùng « some ».

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: « We don't have ___ time left. Hurry up! »
questions.explanation: « Time » (thời gian) là danh từ không đếm được, và trong câu phủ định ta thường dùng « much ».

questions.prompt: Chọn câu đúng:
options: There are a lot of oranges.
There is a lot of oranges.
questions.explanation: « Oranges » là danh từ số nhiều nên dùng « There are », và « a lot of » đi được với danh từ đếm được.

questions.prompt: Câu « Are there any sugar in the jar? » là câu đúng.
questions.explanation: « Sugar » không đếm được nên động từ chia số ít. Câu đúng là « Is there any sugar in the jar? »

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: « You have a cold. You ___ stay at home and rest. »
questions.explanation: Khi khuyên ai nên làm gì, em dùng « should + động từ nguyên mẫu ». Bị cảm thì nên ở nhà nghỉ ngơi.

questions.prompt: « I have a toothache. » nghĩa là gì?
questions.explanation: « Tooth » là răng, « ache » là cơn đau, nên « toothache » là đau răng. Đau đầu là « headache » em nhé.

questions.prompt: Sau « should » ta dùng động từ nguyên mẫu không có « to ».
questions.explanation: Đúng rồi! Ví dụ: « You should drink more water. », không nói « should to drink ».

questions.prompt: Bạn em bị « sunburn » (cháy nắng). Lời khuyên nào phù hợp?
options: You should stay out of the sun.
You should play outside at noon.
questions.explanation: Bị cháy nắng thì nên tránh ánh nắng mặt trời: « You should stay out of the sun. »

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: « You ___ eat too much junk food. It's bad for your health. »
questions.explanation: Đồ ăn vặt có hại cho sức khỏe nên em khuyên « shouldn't » (không nên). « Must to » và « should to » đều sai ngữ pháp.

questions.prompt: Câu « You should to drink more water. » là câu đúng.
questions.explanation: Sau « should » không có « to ». Câu đúng là « You should drink more water. »

questions.prompt: Bạn em bị « chapped lips » (môi nứt nẻ). Hoàn thành lời khuyên: « You should ___. »
options: sit in the sun all day
questions.explanation: Môi nứt nẻ thì nên dùng son dưỡng môi: « You should use lip balm. »

questions.prompt: Cụm từ nào chỉ một thói quen TỐT cho sức khỏe?
questions.explanation: « Doing exercise » (tập thể dục) giúp em khỏe mạnh. Các thói quen còn lại đều có hại.

questions.prompt: « What's the matter? » – « I have a headache. » Lời khuyên phù hợp là:
options: You should listen to loud music.
questions.explanation: Bị đau đầu thì nên nghỉ ngơi: « You should take a rest. » Nghe nhạc to hay thức khuya sẽ làm đau đầu thêm.

questions.prompt: « Sore throat » nghĩa là đau lưng.
questions.explanation: « Sore throat » là đau họng. Đau lưng là « backache » em nhé.

questions.prompt: Chọn câu đúng vị trí của « always »:
options: I get always up at six.
I always get up at six.
I get up always at six.
Always I get up at six.
questions.explanation: Trạng từ chỉ tần suất đứng trước động từ thường, nên « always » đứng trước « get up ».

questions.prompt: Sắp xếp thành câu đúng: « late / is / never / Tom / for school »
options: Tom is never late for school.
Never Tom is late for school.
Tom is late never for school.
Tom is late for school never.
questions.explanation: Trạng từ chỉ tần suất đứng sau động từ « to be », nên « never » đứng sau « is ».

questions.prompt: Trạng từ chỉ tần suất thường đứng trước động từ thường và đứng sau động từ « to be ».
questions.explanation: Đúng rồi! Ví dụ: « She often reads books. » và « She is often happy. »

questions.prompt: « Turn on » nghĩa là gì?
questions.explanation: « Turn on » là bật (đèn, TV...). Tắt là « turn off », tìm kiếm là « look for », thức dậy là « get up ».

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: « I can't find my keys. Can you help me look ___ them? »
questions.explanation: « Look for » nghĩa là tìm kiếm. Không tìm thấy chìa khóa nên em nhờ bạn « look for » giúp.

questions.prompt: « Never » có nghĩa là « luôn luôn ».
questions.explanation: « Never » nghĩa là không bao giờ. « Luôn luôn » là « always » em nhé.

questions.prompt: Trạng từ nào chỉ tần suất CAO NHẤT?
questions.explanation: « Always » (luôn luôn) là mức cao nhất. Thứ tự giảm dần: always > usually > often > sometimes > rarely > never.

questions.prompt: Chọn cụm từ đúng: « It's cold outside. ___ your coat before you go out. »
questions.explanation: « Put on » là mặc vào. Trời lạnh thì phải mặc áo khoác trước khi ra ngoài.

questions.prompt: « Give up » nghĩa là gì?
questions.explanation: « Give up » là từ bỏ, ví dụ « Don't give up! » (Đừng bỏ cuộc!). Lớn lên là « grow up ».

questions.prompt: « How often do you play badminton? » – « Twice a week. » là cặp hỏi – đáp đúng.
questions.explanation: Chính xác! « How often » hỏi về mức độ thường xuyên, nên trả lời « Twice a week » (hai lần một tuần) là hợp lý.

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: « Yesterday, I ___ my old friend at the market and we ___ a lot. »
questions.explanation: Có « yesterday » nên cả hai động từ đều ở quá khứ đơn: « meet » bất quy tắc → « met », « talk » có quy tắc → « talked ».

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: « How ___ sugar did you put in the cake? »
questions.explanation: « Sugar » là danh từ không đếm được nên em hỏi số lượng bằng « How much ».

questions.prompt: Câu « She doesn't usually eats fast food. » là câu đúng.
questions.explanation: Sau « doesn't » động từ phải ở dạng nguyên mẫu. Câu đúng là « She doesn't usually eat fast food. »

questions.prompt: Chọn lời khuyên đúng ngữ pháp:
options: You should goes to bed early.
You shoulds go to bed early.
You should go to bed early.
You should going to bed early.
questions.explanation: « Should » không thêm « s » và luôn đi với động từ nguyên mẫu: « You should go to bed early. »

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: « When I was in Ha Noi last week, I ___ a lot of photos but I didn't ___ any souvenirs. »
questions.explanation: Câu khẳng định quá khứ dùng « took » (quá khứ của take), còn sau « didn't » phải dùng động từ nguyên mẫu « buy ».

questions.prompt: Câu « There weren't many traffic on the road this morning. » là câu đúng.
questions.explanation: « Traffic » là danh từ không đếm được, nên câu đúng là « There wasn't much traffic on the road this morning. »

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: « My brother hardly ever ___ up early on Sundays. »
questions.explanation: Câu nói về thói quen ở hiện tại đơn, chủ ngữ « my brother » là ngôi thứ ba số ít nên động từ thêm « s »: gets.

questions.prompt: Chọn câu đúng:
options: How much money do you have?
How many money do you have?
How much moneys do you have?
How many moneys do you have?
questions.explanation: « Money » là danh từ không đếm được, không thêm « s » và đi với « How much ».

questions.prompt: « Did you turn off the lights before you left? » – « Yes, I ___. »
questions.explanation: Câu hỏi bắt đầu bằng « Did » nên câu trả lời ngắn dùng « did »: Yes, I did.

questions.prompt: Trong câu « You shouldn't eat too many sweets. », ta dùng « many » vì « sweets » là danh từ đếm được.
questions.explanation: Đúng rồi! « Sweets » (kẹo) đếm được và ở số nhiều, nên đi với « many ».

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: « I have lived in this city ___ 2015. »
questions.explanation: « 2015 » là một mốc thời gian, nên em dùng « since » (kể từ).

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: « She has studied English ___ five years. »
questions.explanation: « Five years » là một khoảng thời gian, nên em dùng « for » (trong khoảng).

questions.prompt: « Have you ever been to Da Lat? » là câu hỏi ở thì hiện tại hoàn thành.
questions.explanation: Đúng rồi! Câu có dạng « Have + chủ ngữ + V3 », và « ever » hỏi về trải nghiệm đã từng.

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: « We ___ that film yet. »
questions.explanation: « Yet » trong câu phủ định là dấu hiệu của hiện tại hoàn thành. Chủ ngữ « we » đi với « haven't ».

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: « My father ___ to Japan last year. »
questions.explanation: « Last year » là thời điểm xác định trong quá khứ, nên em dùng quá khứ đơn « went », không dùng hiện tại hoàn thành.

questions.prompt: Câu « She has visited Hue last month. » là câu đúng.
questions.explanation: Có « last month » (thời điểm xác định) nên phải dùng quá khứ đơn: « She visited Hue last month. »

questions.prompt: Quá khứ phân từ (V3) của « write » là gì?
questions.explanation: « Write » là động từ bất quy tắc: write → wrote → written. Thì hiện tại hoàn thành dùng V3 « written ».

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: « I haven't finished my project ___. »
questions.explanation: « Yet » (chưa) dùng ở cuối câu phủ định thì hiện tại hoàn thành. « Already » dùng trong câu khẳng định em nhé.

questions.prompt: Chọn câu đúng:
questions.explanation: Cấu trúc đúng là « has + never + V3 ». Chủ ngữ « he » đi với « has », và V3 của « eat » là « eaten ».

questions.prompt: « For » dùng trước một mốc thời gian, ví dụ « for 2020 ».
questions.explanation: « For » đi với khoảng thời gian (for two years). Mốc thời gian thì dùng « since »: since 2020.

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: « If it ___ tomorrow, we will stay at home. »
questions.explanation: Câu điều kiện loại 1: mệnh đề « if » dùng hiện tại đơn. Chủ ngữ « it » nên động từ thêm « s »: rains.

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: « If you study hard, you ___ the exam. »
questions.explanation: Mệnh đề chính của câu điều kiện loại 1 dùng « will + động từ nguyên mẫu »: you will pass.

questions.prompt: Trong câu điều kiện loại 1, mệnh đề « if » dùng thì hiện tại đơn.
questions.explanation: Đúng rồi! Công thức: If + hiện tại đơn, S + will + V nguyên mẫu.

questions.prompt: « Unless » có nghĩa tương đương với:
questions.explanation: « Unless » nghĩa là « trừ khi », tương đương « if ... not » (nếu ... không).

questions.prompt: Câu « If she will come, I will tell her the news. » là câu đúng.
questions.explanation: Mệnh đề « if » không dùng « will ». Câu đúng là « If she comes, I will tell her the news. »

questions.prompt: Chọn từ đúng: « ___ you hurry, you will miss the bus. »
questions.explanation: « Unless you hurry » nghĩa là « nếu em không nhanh lên », khi đó em sẽ lỡ xe buýt. Câu dùng « Unless » mới hợp nghĩa.

questions.prompt: Chọn câu đúng:
options: If we will recycle more, we reduce waste.
